issues.legal_issue: An unreasoned arbitral award is not invalid per se, and a special leave appeal should not be postponed to await a larger bench when the challenge is raised for the first time at that stage in an old dispute.
material_facts: The objection that the award was invalid for lack of reasons had not been raised before the trial court, the High Court, or in the original objections to the award; it was raised for the first time in the special leave petition.
The dispute and adjudication were old, and the appellant sought to await a pending larger-bench decision on the validity of unreasoned awards.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to postpone the appeal and rejected the contention that the award was invalid merely because it gave no reasons.
issues.legal_principle: As the law then stood, an award without reasons was not bad per se and could be set aside only for misconduct or an error of law apparent on its face. In exercising its discretion under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court would not prolong or unsettle an old arbitration merely because a larger bench was considering the issue, particularly where the objection was raised for the first time in the special leave proceedings.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_reviewing_an_arbitral_award and award_gives_no_reasons and challenge_first_raised_in_special_leave_proceedings and dispute_is_old and request_to_await_larger_bench_decision

predicates.special_leave_appeal_reviewing_an_arbitr: A party seeks special leave to challenge a court decision concerning an arbitral award.
predicates.award_gives_no_reasons: The arbitrator issued an award without stating reasons.
predicates.challenge_first_raised_in_special_leave_: The party first objected to the absence of reasons in the special leave proceedings, rather than in the earlier objections or courts.
predicates.dispute_is_old: The arbitration dispute and its adjudication had already become old.
predicates.request_to_await_larger_bench_decision: The party asked the Court to defer deciding the appeal until a larger bench decided the general issue of unreasoned awards.

issues.definition: When a party first objects to an unreasoned award in a special leave appeal concerning an old dispute and asks the Court to await a larger-bench decision, the objection does not justify postponing the appeal or invalidating the award for lack of reasons alone.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual provision reserving specified decisions to an official does not exclude arbitration of claims that do not fall within those specified matters.
material_facts: The contract provided for arbitration of disputes arising out of or relating to the contract, except where the contract provided otherwise.
A separate clause made an official's decision final on specified matters, including disputes about rates, completion time, and the proportion of additional work to original work.
The arbitrator decided claims for alleged additional work, and the Court found that the claims decided were not among the matters reserved by the separate clause.
issues.conclusion: The reserved-matters clause did not apply to the claims decided by the arbitrator, and the claims were not excluded from arbitration on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The contract's reservation of final decision-making authority must be read together with its arbitration clause. Only disputes falling within the specific matters reserved by the contract are excluded from arbitration. The Court referred to State of Orissa v. Gokulchandra Kanungo and distinguished Bombay Housing Board v. Karbhase Naik & Co., Chief Administrator, Dandakaranya Project v. Prabartak Commercial Corporation, and Food Corporation of India v. P.L. Juneja on the wording of their contracts and the nature of the disputes involved.

predicates.contractual_arbitration_scope_dispute: A party challenges whether a dispute arising under a contract may be decided by arbitration.
predicates.contract_reserves_final_decisions_on_def: The contract assigns final decision-making authority to a specified person for particular categories of disputes.
predicates.claim_is_outside_reserved_matters: The claim decided by the arbitrator does not fall within the categories assigned to that person.

issues.definition: If a contract reserves only defined matters for final decision by another person and the arbitrated claim falls outside those matters, the reservation does not exclude that claim from arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: The size of an arbitral award, without more, does not make the award invalid when the award is not shown to be defective on its face and the circumstances support the amount awarded.
material_facts: The award for additional work was challenged as disproportionately high in light of the payments already made.
Additional work had been performed, and substantial payments had previously been made for such work.
The parties had due opportunities to present evidence before the arbitrator.
The arbitrator was a highly qualified person, and the Court found that the award was not so disproportionate as to shock the Court's conscience.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge based on the amount of the award; the award was not invalid merely because the amount was high.
issues.legal_principle: When parties choose an arbitrator, a mistake of law or fact that does not appear on the face of the award or documents incorporated into it is not a ground to remit or set aside the award. A high award amount alone does not vitiate an award, although evidence of systemic abuse may warrant careful scrutiny in an individual case. The Court relied on Union of India v. Bungo Steel Furniture Pvt. Ltd. and Allen Berry & Co. (P) Ltd. v. Union of India, and referred to State of Orissa v. Gangaram Chhapolia concerning scrutiny where there is evidence of an arbitration racket.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_arbitral_award_as_excessive and award_amount_is_high and additional_work_was_performed and parties_had_opportunity_to_present_evidence and award_is_not_shown_to_be_shocking_in_context

predicates.appeal_challenging_arbitral_award_as_exc: A party appeals from a decision upholding an arbitral award and argues that the amount awarded is excessive.
predicates.award_amount_is_high: The amount granted by the arbitrator is large in relation to the work or payments discussed in the dispute.
predicates.additional_work_was_performed: The contractor performed additional work that formed part of the claims before the arbitrator.
predicates.parties_had_opportunity_to_present_evide: Both parties were given due opportunities to place evidence before the arbitrator.
predicates.award_is_not_shown_to_be_shocking_in_con: The circumstances do not show that the award is so disproportionate as to shock the court's conscience.

issues.definition: Where an award is challenged as excessive, a high amount does not by itself invalidate it if additional work was performed, both parties could present evidence, and the amount is not shown to be shocking in context.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator has no jurisdiction to award interest for the period during which the arbitration is pending.
material_facts: The arbitrator awarded interest that included the period before the award was made.
The award was under review, and the Court identified the interest for the period during the arbitration as interest pendente lite.
issues.conclusion: The Court deleted the interest awarded for the period during the arbitration while sustaining the interest granted from the date of the court decree.
issues.legal_principle: Interest pendente lite is outside an arbitrator's jurisdiction. The Court followed Executive Engineer (Irrigation), Balimela v. Abhaduta Jena, which held that an arbitrator could not grant such interest.

predicates.appeal_reviewing_arbitral_award: A court is reviewing an arbitral award on appeal.
predicates.arbitrator_awarded_interest_for_period_d: The arbitrator included interest for the period between the commencement of arbitration and the award.

issues.definition: If an appeal reviewing an arbitral award finds that the arbitrator granted interest for the period during the arbitration, that interest must be deleted.
